C0.quote: we study the complexity of deciding whether voters' preferences can be explained
C0.note: Borderline: computational problem on preference profiles (structured domains) motivated by voting; no rule defined. Coded ELIG as computational aspects of voting.

C1.note: Polynomial algorithms and NP-hardness for partitioning profiles.

C2.1.quote: A preference profile P over a candidate set C is a list of votes

C2.2.quote: A vote over C is a linear order over C.

C2.3.quote: each voter has a preferred value for each attribute
C2.3.note: Paper speaks of voters' preferences, favorite points and decision-making.

C2.4.note: Preferences described as votes/profiles; no statement on submission or reporting.

C4.1.note: No utility-type notions used for voters.

VOT.note: No agent takes an action in the formal model; the profile is an input to a decision problem.
